Very poor experience here.

We arrived expecting a straightforward check in after travelling over 10 hours from the UK with our baby. What followed was one of the most stressful hotel experiences we have had.

There were no staff on site when we arrived. Guests are directed to pay at a self service machine next to a restaurant where your room key is activated.

When we reached our room, we realised there was no cot despite having requested one in advance as we were travelling with an infant.

I went back downstairs and found a sign stating that there are no staff on site after 12pm and that guests must contact a WhatsApp number if assistance is required.

After waiting for a reply, we were told via WhatsApp that nobody was available to help until the following day. There was no attempt to resolve the situation.

All communication was via WhatsApp and the language and tone of the messages were extremely poor. The responses were badly written, informal and did not read like communication from a professionally run hotel.

“Sorry about that , contact you three party and request de refund”

At a time when we needed urgent help, it felt unreliable and deeply concerning.

There was no manager, no night staff and no one physically present who could assist. We were left messaging someone remotely who could not offer any practical solution.

With no safe sleeping arrangement for our baby, staying was not an option. Late in the evening, we had to find and book alternative accommodation.

At the time, we were told that a note would be sent to management to arrange a refund. We felt reassured that although chaotic, the situation would at least be handled fairly.

After ignoring follow up messages and emails for a six days, the hotel finally came back (again via WhatsApp) and refused to refund us. Despite informing them within an hour of check in that we had been forced to leave, they now claim the room was technically available for the duration of the stay and that a cot is not guaranteed, despite advertising free cots available on request.

The combination of no on site staff, remote only messaging and unprofessional communication left us feeling extremely uncomfortable and unsupported.

We would strongly caution others before booking. Try the Plymouth hotel instead - they were great and it actually feels like a boutique hotel.

I have stayed here twice before, and while it wasn’t great, it was tolerable. After this most recent stay, however, I will never return. This was the worst hotel experience I have ever had.

We reserved a king room but were assigned room 311, which had two full beds instead. When I spoke to the front desk, I was told the only other available room had a moldy smell and that there were no other rooms to switch to.

In room 311, the air conditioning was “master controlled,” and we were unable to lower it below 74 degrees. We asked the front desk for help, and the employee truly did everything she could. She even showed us that her system would not allow the temperature to be set any lower. By morning, the room was 81 degrees and extremely humid. I honestly would have rather slept outside. I have never stayed at a hotel where you can’t control the temp yourself...it’s completely unacceptable.

The bed sheets didn’t fit properly, and every time you sat down, one corner would come loose. The carpets were also extremely dirty, so we wore shoes the entire time.

I want to emphasize that the front desk employee was very helpful, apologetic, and did her best to resolve the issues. It’s clear this is not a staff problem, but a result of ownership failing to properly maintain and manage the property.

I stayed at the hotel for a week with my fiancé. Until checkout, we were genuinely happy with our stay, so much so that I even encouraged a friend to book a room there as well. Unfortunately, the way the hotel handled a simple lost item completely changed my impression.

After checking out on Saturday morning, we left our luggage at the hotel as our flight was later that evening. Around two hours after checkout, I realised I had left a shirt hanging on the bathroom door hook. My fiancé immediately called the hotel, but the call was disconnected…tried to call minimum 5 times after that - no answer.

When we returned to collect our luggage, I informed reception about the item. The staff member immediately stated that nothing had been found - without checking. Only after I insisted did she go to speak with housekeeping. She then returned and repeated that nothing had been found.

I am absolutely certain where I left the shirt. While it had little monetary value, it was a sentimental souvenir from travels. What is most disappointing is not the loss itself, but the dismissive and unprofessional way the situation was handled. There was no genuine attempt to assist, no empathy, and no accountability.

It is frustrating to leave what was otherwise a pleasant stay with the feeling that concerns are dismissed rather than properly addressed. Unfortunately, this experience has significantly affected my overall impression of the hotel.

text.text:
Fairwind Hotel Miami (1000 Collins Ave) | Clean and well-located, but fee transparency and basic functionality need work.

I stayed one night on Feb 6 (pre-cruise) and the biggest positives were the location and cleanliness. The hotel is in the heart of South Beach to walkable restaurants and about a block from the beach. My room was immaculately clean, and the 20% discount at the on-site restaurants with your room key was a nice perk.

That said, the experience was held back by several issues. At check-in, you pay a $35 resort fee that I did not see disclosed when booking, along with a $100 incidental hold. Also, the payment kiosks were down, and the manager said he had to manually enter my card, which created unnecessary concern.

The room (212) was much smaller than the online photos suggested and lacked basic functionality: no chair and no desk. The bathroom setup was awkward: the vent was positioned over the toilet rather than the shower, towel racks were placed over/near the toilet instead of by the shower (so you have to step out and walk to retrieve towels), and there were no power outlets in the bathroom, so shaving/grooming had to be done by the bed. The sink also drained very slowly. I reported it and was told someone would come up, but no one ever did. Bathroom lack shelving or counter top space.

Overall, it served its purpose for a quick overnight before heading to PortMiami, but the surprise fees, room mismatch, and lack of follow-through on service make it hard to rate higher.

Overall: solid 3.5 stars

The good:
•	Location is perfect. You’re one block from the beach and in the middle of everything.
•	Service was genuinely excellent. Check-in with Melody was great, she was friendly, welcoming, and went out of her way to get us into a room early. We arrived on a morning flight fully expecting to wait until the official check-in time, so being able to shower and reset right away was a big deal.
•	Amenities are impressive for South Beach. Beach towels and chairs, bikes for rent, gym passes, water, coffee, etc. Not every hotel in the area offers that without nickel-and-diming.
•	Housekeeping was solid. Daily cleanup, nicely refreshed room, and bottled water (oddly 2 out of 3 days but still appreciated).
•	Bathroom was great. Spacious shower and good water pressure.

What needs work:
•	Noise insulation is basically non-existent. Besides the usual Ocean Drive evening noise, our room was directly above a bar that blasted repetitive music with the same beat over and over- enough to drive anyone insane when you’re trying to sleep. At minimum they should offer proper earplugs for families or light sleepers.
•	Rooms are on the smaller side (fine for a couple, tight for a family of 3), and the layout is odd. There’s a little entry area separated by doors from the sleeping space, which is nice, but then there’s a transparent glass wall between that area and the shower. With a teenage daughter, it meant constantly watching who was going where while someone was showering or using the restroom.
•	We were placed in the building next door, not the main hotel building. To reach our room we had to walk through the “Naked Taco” restaurant, which takes up the entire lobby. The smell inside that lobby was honestly awful: a mix of throw-up, spilled liquor, and sewage. All three of us commented on it every single time. The main building lobby smelled fine, so I wish we’d been placed there instead. They really need to address the ventilation/cleanliness because no hotel guest wants that.
•	Pool is just okay. Nice to have, but only 3 ft deep and feels more like a bar/drinking scene than an actual pool where adults can swim or relax.

Bottom line:
Great location, great staff, surprisingly good amenities for South Beach, but noise, layout quirks, and that awful restaurant smell hold it back. If we stayed again, we’d only do it with a room in the main building and away from the bar
